newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe airlines raise domestic fares.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe airlines raise domestic fares.

text.p: State-owned Air Zimbabwe and the privately-run Zimbabwe Express Airlines (ZEX) said on Tuesday they would raise their domestic airfares by 30 percent from September 1 to meet rising operational costs.

In a joint statement, the two airlines said the move was necessary to maintain the viability of domestic flights in the face of increased jet fuel prices which had gone up twice in the past year as well as higher landing and navigation fees.
"The domestic fares charged are so low that were it not for the support from other routes, the airlines' domestic operations would not be viable," the statement said.
ZEX broke a monopoly formerly held by the state airline when it started operating domestic and regional flights in 1995.
Earlier this year, a second private airline -- Expedition Airways -- also took to the skies, bringing the number of local airlines to three.
